title: Warriors forward suspended one game after sideline exchange with teammate
body: Golden State suspended Draymond Green for one game without pay following a heated exchange with Kevin Durant in the closing seconds of a loss to the Clippers. The two continued arguing in the locker room afterward, according to multiple people present. Green had refused to give up the ball on the final possession, and the disagreement escalated into a personal confrontation. Durant declined to characterise the incident publicly, saying only that the team would handle it internally. He left the franchise the following summer.
retrieval_note: Describes a conflict without ever using the word 'beef'. Keyword search for 'beef' misses this entirely.

title: Video surfaces of practice altercation between Warriors guards
body: A recording of a physical altercation during a closed Golden State practice was published by a national outlet, showing Draymond Green striking Jordan Poole. The team fined Green and he stepped away from the facility for several days. Poole was traded to Washington the following offseason in a deal widely read as a consequence of the incident. Neither player addressed the specifics on the record.
retrieval_note: A graph query can connect this incident to the trade that followed it. Text search alone cannot make that causal link.

title: Two ejected, one suspended after scuffle at Target Center
body: A first-quarter scuffle between Minnesota and Golden State ended with Draymond Green pulling Rudy Gobert into a headlock and dragging him away from a confrontation between Kyle Anderson and a Warriors teammate. Green was suspended five games, the longest suspension handed down that month. Gobert said afterward he had been trying to separate players, not escalate. Anderson, who was at the centre of the original push, was fined but not suspended.
retrieval_note: Three participants, two distinct conflict pairs. Graph search distinguishes them; keyword search returns one undifferentiated blob.

title: Timberwolves star confronts teammates in charged practice session
body: Weeks after requesting a trade, Jimmy Butler returned to practice and joined the third unit, which proceeded to beat the starters. Butler directed pointed criticism at Karl-Anthony Towns and the front office during and after the session. He was traded to Philadelphia within two months. Towns later described the period as the most difficult of his career.
retrieval_note: The word 'beef' never appears, but this is one of the best-known interpersonal disputes in the dataset.

title: Celtics guard criticises younger teammates after home loss
body: Kyrie Irving told reporters that Boston's younger players did not yet understand what it takes to win at the highest level, singling out the group's inexperience. Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown responded carefully when asked the next day. The comments deepened an already visible rift inside a team that had entered the season with championship expectations. Irving left in free agency that summer.
retrieval_note: Uses 'rift', not 'beef' or 'feud'. Semantic search finds it; exact keyword search for conflict terms does not.

title: Sixers big man and new wing clashed over shot distribution, sources say
body: Philadelphia's half-court offense produced repeated disagreements between Joel Embiid and Jimmy Butler over who should initiate late in games. Butler pushed for more pick-and-roll possessions with himself as the handler; the coaching staff kept running the offense through the post. The tension never became public during the season but shaped the front office's decision not to build around the pairing. Butler was sign-and-traded to Miami weeks later.
retrieval_note: Refers to Embiid as 'big man' in the headline only. The structured position field is the reliable path.

title: Finals suspension changes the series after Game 4 altercation
body: Draymond Green was suspended for Game 5 of the Finals after accumulating a flagrant foul point in an altercation with LeBron James, who stepped over him during a dead ball. Cleveland won the game and eventually the series after trailing 3-1. Both players later said the exchange was competitive rather than personal. It remains the most consequential suspension in Finals history.
retrieval_note: A conflict between players who were never teammates. Useful for showing that graph traversal depth matters.

title: Star forward responds to critics from an unmarked account
body: Kevin Durant acknowledged replying to online critics from accounts that did not carry his name, after several replies were posted from his verified profile by mistake. He called it immature and said he took responsibility. The episode became a long-running reference point in discussions of his relationship with public criticism.
retrieval_note: A single-participant conflict event. Graph queries that assume two participants will silently miss it.

title: Blazers guard requests trade after eleven seasons
body: Damian Lillard formally requested a trade from Portland and communicated a single preferred destination through his representation. The front office stated publicly that it would not be constrained by that preference. Lillard was dealt to Milwaukee in September in a three-team transaction. The episode became a reference case in debates about how much leverage a player under contract actually holds.
retrieval_note: A dispute with an organisation rather than a person. Ontology reasoning is what links 'ContractDispute' to the broader 'Conflict' class.

title: Knicks forward gestures to the crowd after another loss
body: Julius Randle gave a thumbs-down gesture toward the Madison Square Garden crowd following a made basket, later explaining he wanted the fans to stop booing the team. He apologised the following day. The moment became shorthand for a difficult season in New York.
retrieval_note: Contains no conflict vocabulary at all. Only the ontology's mapping of 'PublicCallout' to Conflict retrieves it.

title: Knicks big man asks out in meeting, dealt within days
body: Kristaps Porzingis met with New York's front office and told them he wanted to be traded, citing the direction of the franchise. He was moved to Dallas two days later in a deal that returned two first-round picks and salary relief. The speed of the transaction surprised even people inside the building.
retrieval_note: Connects a conflict event directly to a trade event. That join is trivial in a graph and awkward in text.

title: Grizzlies guard suspended 25 games for off-court conduct
body: The league suspended Ja Morant for the first 25 games of the following season after a second incident involving a firearm on social media. Memphis supported the ruling and said Morant would work with the team on a return plan. The suspension cost him roughly a third of the season and a significant portion of his salary.
retrieval_note: A disciplinary event, not an interpersonal dispute. Naive semantic search for 'player conflicts' surfaces it as a false positive.

title: The Green-Gobert beef, explained
body: The two have traded criticism in interviews for years, mostly about defensive value and awards voting. The headlock at Target Center was the physical expression of an argument that had been running verbally since at least the 2017 Defensive Player of the Year vote. Neither has shown much interest in de-escalating. This explainer traces the timeline from awards-season sniping to on-court contact.
retrieval_note: The only conflict document that literally contains the word 'beef'. Keyword search for 'beef' ranks this first and finds almost nothing else useful.

title: Nets guard requests trade during extension talks
body: Kyrie Irving asked Brooklyn for a trade after extension negotiations stalled over guarantees and length. He was dealt to Dallas three days later. His departure preceded Kevin Durant's own trade request by less than a week, and the two moves ended Brooklyn's superteam era in a single deadline cycle.
retrieval_note: Two trade requests days apart by former teammates. The graph makes the pattern visible; a text index does not.

title: Brisket, not beef: inside Ball Arena's smokehouse operation
body: Ball Arena's kitchen smokes roughly two thousand pounds of beef brisket per home stand, a program that began as a single cart behind section 114. The head chef sources from three Colorado ranches and finishes each cut over local applewood. Fans queue for up to forty minutes at the busiest windows. The beef program now outsells every other concession item in the building.
retrieval_note: TRAP: contains 'beef' three times and has nothing to do with player conflicts. Keyword search for 'beef' ranks this highly. Semantic search discards it.

title: Beef Wellington and the pregame ritual that outlasted three coaches
body: A Boston-area caterer has prepared the same pregame beef Wellington for the visiting bench at TD Garden since 2011. Three head coaches have come and gone; the order has not changed. Players rarely eat it, but the tradition survives because nobody wants to be the one to cancel it.
retrieval_note: TRAP: another literal 'beef' document. Two of these in the corpus is enough to poison a naive keyword result page.

title: Traction complaints: the friction between new court finishes and modern soles
body: Several teams have raised concerns about the coefficient of friction between resurfaced hardwood and the low-profile outsoles now common across signature lines. Equipment managers report more slips in the first weeks after a resurface. The league has begun logging friction measurements at each arena. No rule change is under consideration.
retrieval_note: TRAP: 'friction' used in its literal physical sense. Keyword search for 'friction' as a conflict synonym returns this.

title: Trade secrets: what a shooting coach actually changes in a jumper
body: The most common intervention is not the release but the feet. A shooting coach describes rebuilding Desmond Bane's base without touching a stroke that scouts once called mechanically unorthodox. The trade secrets of the profession are mostly patience and video. Most changes take two full offseasons to hold under fatigue.
retrieval_note: TRAP: 'trade' appears in an idiom, not as a transaction. Keyword search for 'trade' surfaces it above real transaction records.

title: Bad Blood: a new documentary revisits the rivalries of the 1980s
body: A four-part documentary series revisits the Celtics-Lakers rivalry through the players who lived it. The bad blood of that era, the filmmakers argue, was partly manufactured by a league that needed a narrative. Archival footage includes previously unaired locker room audio. No current players appear.
retrieval_note: TRAP: 'bad blood' and 'rivalries' with zero connection to any player in the database. Semantic search for player feuds ranks it uncomfortably high.

title: Beefing up: how one center added fifteen pounds without losing a step
body: Bam Adebayo spent the offseason adding mass to hold position against heavier post players without sacrificing his ability to switch onto guards. The program was built around eccentric loading rather than volume. He reported to camp fifteen pounds heavier and posted the same lateral quickness numbers. Beefing up, in his case, meant changing what he ate more than what he lifted.
retrieval_note: TRAP: 'beefing up' is an idiom about weight training. It also demonstrates that 'center' and 'big man' need ontology mapping, not string matching.

title: The seven-footer who shoots like a guard
body: Karl-Anthony Towns takes more than six three-point attempts per game and converts them at a rate that would rank near the top among starting guards. He plays next to a traditional five, which pushes him to the perimeter on most possessions. The pairing was widely criticised when it was assembled. Three seasons later it produces one of the better half-court offenses in the conference.
retrieval_note: Says 'seven-footer' and 'five', never 'center' or 'power forward'. Ontology-backed retrieval maps all of these to the same class.

title: Rim protection is still the cheapest defense you can buy
body: Teams with a designated rim protector concede meaningfully fewer points per possession at the basket, and the effect survives controlling for perimeter personnel. Brook Lopez, Rudy Gobert and Anthony Davis anchor three of the four stingiest interior defenses. The archetype has been declared obsolete roughly once per season for a decade. It keeps winning playoff series.
retrieval_note: 'Rim protector' is a defined ontology class (blocks per game plus position). No literal position string appears in the text.

title: Every unprotected first-round pick changing hands this cycle
body: Four unprotected firsts moved in the Durant deal and four more in the Gobert deal, concentrating future risk in two franchises. Both packages were assembled during a window in which teams were willing to trade unprotected equity for immediate contention. The compounding effect on those two rosters is now visible. Neither team controls its own first-round pick in three of the next five drafts.
retrieval_note: Draft-pick flows are edges, not text. A graph query returns the actual pick ledger; this article only summarises it.

title: Deadline day: the moves that actually changed a rotation
body: Dallas added a vertical finisher and immediately posted its best offensive stretch of the season. New York's midseason wing acquisition produced a defensive improvement of comparable size. Most deadline deals do not move a rotation. These two did, and both were completed for a single protected or unprotected first.
retrieval_note: Mentions players by role rather than name in the lede. Semantic search handles the paraphrase; keyword search needs the exact names.

title: Undrafted to starter: the path that keeps getting shorter
body: Austin Reaves went undrafted and started in a conference final within two seasons. Jalen Brunson was taken thirty-third and became a first-team All-NBA guard. Both cases point to the same inefficiency in draft evaluation: production against good competition remains undervalued relative to measurable athleticism. Front offices say they have corrected for it. The evidence is mixed.
retrieval_note: Structured query territory: 'draft_pick IS NULL OR draft_pick > 30'. Text search cannot express that filter.

title: The passing big man is no longer an exception
body: Elbow-based offense run through a post player now accounts for a growing share of half-court possessions league-wide. Nikola Jokic averages nine assists, a figure no player his size had previously sustained. The archetype spread quickly because it solves a specific problem: it lets a team keep five shooters on the floor while still having a hub. Defenses have not found a stable answer.
retrieval_note: 'Big man' in the title, but the players referenced hold three different position codes. Only ontology expansion catches all of them.

title: Contract year economics and the no-trade clause nobody else has
body: A full no-trade clause has been granted to exactly one active player under the current agreement. It reshaped Washington's leverage in every conversation about the roster. Phoenix absorbed the contract anyway, betting that on-court fit would outweigh future flexibility. The bet constrained the front office for the following two offseasons.
retrieval_note: Salary and contract structure are structured fields. A SQL query answers this precisely; the article only gestures at it.

title: Two MVPs, one shot profile, opposite conclusions
body: One takes almost nothing outside the paint and converts at a historic rate inside it. The other operates from the elbow and passes more than any player at his position ever has. Both won multiple MVP awards within the same five-year window. The comparison is useful mainly because it shows how little the archetype constrains the ceiling.
retrieval_note: Never names either player's position. The structured field is the only reliable filter.

title: Why the stretch five broke the drop coverage
body: When the opposing five can shoot, dropping the defensive big below the level of the screen concedes an open above-the-break three. Boston and Milwaukee both start centers who shoot better than league average from distance, which forces opponents into coverages they would rather not run. The counter has been to switch, which creates the mismatches those teams are built to attack.
retrieval_note: Uses 'five' and 'big' as position words. Keyword search for 'center' returns nothing here.

title: He was traded twice before he turned twenty-six
body: Daniel Gafford has changed teams twice, each time as the secondary piece in a larger deal. He has never requested a move and has never publicly commented on one. His role has been identical in all three stops: screen, roll, finish, protect the rim. The consistency is the point.
retrieval_note: A multi-hop question ('players traded more than once') is a graph traversal, not a text query.

title: The Kentucky pipeline, twelve years on
body: Six current starters came through the same college program within a decade. The pattern reflects recruiting concentration more than developmental method, but the shared vocabulary between them is real. Several have said they still exchange film. The program's alumni now occupy roughly one roster spot in fifteen league-wide.
retrieval_note: A perfect structured query ('GROUP BY college'). Retrieving it as text gives you one article instead of the actual list.

title: International first: the second-round pick who became a three-time MVP
body: Selected forty-first overall, Nikola Jokic was the last player taken in the second round to become a perennial MVP candidate. Denver's scouting department had him graded far higher than the market. The gap between his draft position and his production is the largest in the modern era by a wide margin.
retrieval_note: Combines a numeric filter (draft_pick) with a country filter. Hybrid retrieval handles it; pure text does not.

title: Sources: front office split on whether to move the young forward
body: Golden State's decision-makers have not reached consensus on whether to include Jonathan Kuminga in a deal for immediate help. One faction views him as the only tradeable asset of consequence; another sees him as the bridge to the next competitive window. No offer has been formally rejected. The disagreement is internal and has not involved the player.
retrieval_note: An organisational disagreement with no player conflict. Tests whether a retriever can tell 'front office split' from 'player feud'.

title: The quiet part of a superteam breakup
body: Two trade requests six days apart ended a three-year project that never reached a conference final. Neither player publicly criticised the other. People inside the building described a room that had stopped having difficult conversations rather than one that was actively hostile. The absence of open conflict is what made the ending difficult to see coming.
retrieval_note: Describes the ABSENCE of conflict. A semantic search for 'player feuds' will surface it as a false positive.

title: Awards voting and the argument that will not die
body: The Defensive Player of the Year race has produced a recurring public disagreement between two defenders about what the award should measure. One argues for rim deterrence and volume; the other for versatility and the ability to guard the perimeter. The exchange has been conducted through podcasts and postgame interviews for the better part of seven years. It resurfaces every March.
retrieval_note: A slow-burning verbal dispute that predates the physical altercation in n03. The graph can order these events; text search cannot.

title: Return from a five-game suspension
body: Draymond Green returned to the lineup after serving the longest suspension of his career, saying he had used the time to work with a counsellor. He committed no technical fouls in his first three games back. Teammates described the return as measured. The team went 2-1 over that stretch.
retrieval_note: A follow-up document that mentions a suspension but describes no conflict. Keyword search for 'suspension' cannot separate cause from aftermath.

title: Load management, availability and the thirty-nine-year-old
body: A player in his twenty-first season is producing at a level that has no historical comparison, on a minutes plan built backward from the postseason. The Lakers have managed back-to-backs conservatively all year. Availability, not production, has been the constraint on the roster around him.
retrieval_note: Age is a structured field. 'Veteran' is an ontology class defined as age >= 32.

title: The 40 percent club is smaller than you think
body: Fewer than thirty rotation players are converting above forty percent from three on meaningful volume. The list is dominated by guards, with two notable wing exceptions. Volume matters more than percentage below a certain attempt threshold, which is why raw leaderboards mislead. The names that survive both filters are largely the same year over year.
retrieval_note: 'Sniper' is defined in the ontology as fg3_pct >= 0.38. This article gestures at the list; SQL returns it exactly.

title: Injury report: what a calf strain actually costs
body: Soft-tissue injuries to players over two hundred and forty pounds carry longer expected absences and higher recurrence rates than the public timelines suggest. Two of the league's most productive interior players have each missed extended stretches this season. Teams increasingly plan rotations around expected absence rather than reacting to it.
retrieval_note: Filters on weight and position. The text never states either value.

title: He asked to be traded and got the destination wrong
body: A public preference for one destination did not produce that outcome. Portland moved its longest-tenured player to a third team that had not been part of the original conversation. The episode clarified how little a no-trade-clause-free contract constrains a front office. Milwaukee gave up its own future first-round equity to complete the deal.
retrieval_note: Pairs a conflict event with a trade event and a pick transfer. Three node types, one question.

title: Switchability is the whole job now
body: Defenders who can guard three or more positions without a scheme adjustment are the scarcest commodity in roster construction. The three most valuable examples this season each occupy a different nominal position. Nominal position, in fact, has become the least informative thing on a depth chart.
retrieval_note: Explicitly argues that position labels are unreliable, which is exactly the problem an ontology solves.

title: Draft class of 2018: a six-year audit
body: Six years on, the 2018 class has produced one perennial MVP candidate, one Defensive Player of the Year and one All-NBA guard taken thirty-third overall. The top of the class has held up better than most. The order, as usual, has not.
retrieval_note: 'Draft classmate' is a derived relationship, computed from draft_year rather than stored as an edge.

title: Locker room split into camps, sources say
body: Multiple people described a room that had divided into groups that did not communicate outside of scheduled team activities. Veterans and younger players were increasingly running separate routines. No single incident was identified as the cause. The team lost in the second round and the roster was substantially rebuilt that summer.
retrieval_note: Conflict with no conflict vocabulary: no 'beef', 'feud', 'fight', or 'altercation' appears anywhere in the text.

title: Two former teammates meet in the conference finals
body: Both players have changed franchises since they last shared a floor in an All-Star setting. Neither has spoken publicly about the other in months. The matchup is notable mainly because of how much roster movement had to occur for it to happen at all.
retrieval_note: Says 'former teammates' in the title but the two never actually shared a roster in this dataset. Text search believes the headline; the graph does not.
